title: NHIS Health Inequality Trends
summary: Reproducible SAS pipelines and survey harmonization across pooled NHIS data (1997 to 2024), supporting health-inequality research toward a manuscript in preparation.
overview: I build and maintain the survey-harmonization and analytics infrastructure behind a long-running health-inequality study using pooled NHIS data. The work focuses on cross-period comparability, reproducibility, and quality assurance, and supports a manuscript in preparation.
myRole: I lead the harmonization and analytic workflow, focusing on methodological consistency, cross-period comparability, reproducibility, and quality assurance, in coordination with the faculty investigator.

sections.title: Data Harmonization & Reproducibility
content: Harmonized more than two decades of NHIS data across major survey redesigns, resolving changes in variable definitions, coding, and design structures for cross-period comparability.
Built reproducible SAS workflows with consistent naming conventions, version-controlled outputs, and a documented harmonization rulebook.
Established quality-assurance protocols, including drift checks, cross-tab validation, and missingness diagnostics, that catch data issues before analysis.

outcomes: Harmonized more than two decades of NHIS data into an analysis-ready, version-controlled resource.
Built reproducible QA protocols and documentation supporting transparent, replicable research.
